gap.quote: Prior studies have primarily documented this effect in static text domains

A significant gap exists in understanding whether this phenomenon extends to agentic systems, where the transfer involves behavioral tendencies (actions) and policy dynamics rather than static semantic associations.
Standard safety protocols rely on filtering this training data for explicit unsafe content to prevent the propagation of harmful behaviors.

approach.quote: we construct a teacher agent exhibiting a strong deletion bias, a tendency to perform destructive file-system actions via an API-style tool interface, and distill it into a student using only trajectories from ostensibly safe tasks, with all explicit deletion keywords rigorously filtered.
we replicate the threat model in a native Bash environment, replacing API tool calls with shell commands

evaluation.quote: We evaluate the student on a held-out set of ambiguous tasks where deletion is a possible but non-mandated action, and measure the probability of deletion Pdel relative to an unbiased baseline agent.
We compare the distilled student’s deletion propensity against two specific baselines.
Second, the Control Student is a model distilled from a teacher fine-tuned on random benign tasks rather than deletion-specific tasks.
We define the chmod-first rate Pchmod(θ) as the fraction of evaluation tasks in which the agent’s first permission-related command is chmod.

l2.gap: Trait transfer through unrelated data was shown for static text, not for agent behavior.
l2.approach: Train student agents on filtered safe trajectories from a teacher with an unsafe behavioral tendency.
l2.evaluation: Measure unsafe action rates on ambiguous tasks against baseline and control agents.
l2.query_text: Language models can pass traits to student models through data that looks unrelated to those traits, but this has been shown mainly for static text. Can unsafe behavioral tendencies of a teacher agent transfer to a student agent trained on filtered trajectories from safe tasks?

gold.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
gold.evidence_quote: The phenomenon of subliminal trait transfer in LLMs was first systematically characterized by Cloud et al. (2025), who demonstrated that student models trained on semantically unrelated data (e.g., number sequences) from a teacher model can inherit behavioral preferences like entity biases.

gold.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training

gold.evidence_quote: Zur et al. (2025) recently proposed that subliminal transfer in language models operates through ”token entanglement,” where low-probability tokens become statistically correlated with target concepts during training.

gold.evidence_quote: Recent research on agentic mis-alignment demonstrates that autonomous models can act as “insider threats,” engaging in harmful behaviors such as sabotage or blackmail when they perceive threats to their operational continuity (Lynch et al., 2025).
